title: Best Time for a Nile Cruise: Month-by-Month
excerpt: The best time for a Nile cruise is October to April: days of 23 to 36 °C and cool nights. Month-by-month weather and crowds; cruises from €500, Nov 2026.

Quick answer

The best time for a Nile cruise is October to April, when Luxor and Aswan see days of roughly 23 to 36 °C and cool nights. December and January are usually the busiest weeks. June to August brings 41 to 42 °C heat, quieter sites and, across the market, typically the lowest fares (Sawa's own prices do not change by season). November and March are the sweet spot. Within any month, the best time for Nile sightseeing is early morning.

UNESCO documents the temples and necropolis of ancient Thebes, including Luxor and its West Bank.

You have picked the boat, the route and the cabin; now comes the calendar question: which month? The Nile can be cruised all year, but a 41 °C August afternoon and a 7 °C February night are very different holidays. This post gives the full 12-month picture: average temperatures for Luxor and Aswan, the crowd and price patterns, and a clear recommendation. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is a shared-departure marketplace for Egyptian day tours, cruises and packages, founded by an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Best time for a Nile cruise: the short answer

October to April is the best time for a Nile cruise. Luxor and Aswan then see days of roughly 23 to 36 °C, cool nights and almost no rain, so open-air sites stay comfortable. Inside that window, November and March are the sweet spot: warm days and, outside the holidays, fewer crowds. May to September still works for travellers who accept 39 to 42 °C afternoons in exchange for quiet boats and, across the market, typically lower fares.

Nile cruise weather by month: Luxor and Aswan

The table gives average daily highs and lows for Luxor and Aswan (1991 to 2020 climate normals, rounded to the nearest degree), with the usual crowd and price pattern beside them. Rain barely exists: Luxor averages about 8 mm a year, so you plan around heat, not forecasts.

Month Luxor high / low °C Aswan high / low °C Crowds and prices (typical)
January 23 / 7 23 / 10 Peak around Christmas and New Year; easing later in the month
February 25 / 9 26 / 12 Busy to mid-month, then easing
March 30 / 13 30 / 16 Shoulder: warm and comfortable, busier around Easter
April 35 / 18 36 / 20 Shoulder turning hot; occasional hot spring winds
May 39 / 22 40 / 25 Low season begins
June 41 / 25 42 / 27 Low season: very hot, quiet sites
July 41 / 26 42 / 28 Low season: typically the lowest market fares
August 41 / 26 42 / 28 Low season: the hottest month; sightsee at dawn
September 39 / 23 40 / 26 Low season; heat begins to ease late in the month
October 36 / 20 36 / 22 The season picks up again; good value
November 29 / 13 30 / 16 Shoulder turning peak: many travellers' finest month
December 24 / 9 25 / 11 Peak: Christmas and New Year dates fill first

Read the highs first. The big sites open early (the Valley of the Kings opens at 06:00 and closes at 17:00, and Karnak keeps similar hours), and above about 38 °C the shade-free courtyards of Karnak become hard work. In Ramadan, expected to begin around 8 February 2027, opening hours shorten, so check them for February and early March dates. Then read the nights: from November to February, deck dinners need a jumper.

  • Averages hide extremes: the records are about 50 °C in Luxor (in May) and 51 °C in Aswan (in July). June to August can approach those numbers, hence dawn sightseeing in summer.
  • Tombs are out of the sun, but the walk between them is not, so a summer day in the Valley of the Kings is best done at opening time.
  • Twice a year, around 22 February and 22 October, sunrise lights the sanctuary of Ramses II at Abu Simbel, and those weeks fill early. See the Abu Simbel sun festival.

Nile cruise crowds and prices: peak, shoulder and low season

Crowds and prices broadly follow the thermometer, not the river. Mid-December to early January is peak: boats full, flights dear and market prices at their year high. October, November, March and April are the shoulder; May to September is the low season, when boats are quietest and market fares tend to fall furthest.

Two booking realities matter. Christmas, New Year and Easter departures fill months ahead, so reserve those weeks early. And on Sawa the season does not change the price: prices are fixed per traveller and shown on each departure page. As listed in November 2026, the five-day Nile Majesty cruise from Luxor is from €610 and the four-day Nile Discovery cruise from Aswan is from €500, both full board. They are not like-for-like: Nile Discovery includes the Luxor to Cairo flight and a Cairo dinner cruise, while Nile Majesty excludes flights.

A Nile cruise in summer: what 40 °C actually feels like

A Nile cruise in summer is hot but workable if you change the rhythm. June to August averages 41 to 42 °C by day, so the day shrinks to the cool hours: temples at dawn, then the shaded deck (and the pool, if your boat has one) through the afternoon. Nile cruisers are generally air-conditioned; confirm it for your boat.

The honest case for summer is quiet sites and, across the market, typically the year's lowest fares; on Sawa the price is the same in every month. Against it stands noon walking on Karnak's exposed ground and Hatshepsut's terraces. Summer suits early risers, heat-tolerant travellers and anyone watching the budget.

Nile cruise in December: warm days, cold nights

December is a fine month for a Nile cruise, with one catch. Daytime highs sit near 24 °C in Luxor and 25 °C in Aswan, ideal temple weather, but nights fall to 9 to 11 °C and a felucca (a traditional wooden sailboat) ride after sunset feels colder still. Pack layers.

December is also peak season, and Christmas and New Year departures fill first. Days are short, with the sun setting shortly after 5 pm, so sightseeing ends earlier than in spring. Book ahead and keep evenings simple: dinner on board, a jumper, the temples seen by day.

Do water levels affect a Nile cruise?

Barely, which surprises many travellers. The Aswan High Dam, completed in 1970, regulates the river below it, so the old summer flood no longer governs the season and cruises are sold in every month of the year.

What shifts your day is not the water level but the Esna lock, about 55 to 60 km south of Luxor, which every Luxor to Aswan cruise passes. Most ships now pass in around two hours, depending on river traffic, and the queue can move the day's schedule. Scheduled maintenance at the barrage can occasionally affect timings too, so ask your operator whether anything is planned for your dates.

The verdict on the best time for a Nile cruise

For most travellers the best time for a Nile cruise is October to April, with November and March the sweet spot; summer rewards early risers with quiet temples. faq.q: When is the best time for a Nile cruise?
faq.a: In short, October to April. Luxor and Aswan then average days of roughly 23 to 36 °C with cool nights, so temple walking stays comfortable. November and March balance warmth with thinner crowds; mid-December to early January is the busiest stretch. May to September brings 39 to 42 °C heat but the quietest boats, which is workable if you sightsee at dawn.

faq.q: Which months have the lowest Nile cruise prices?
faq.a: Across the market, low season, roughly May to September and deepest in July and August, typically brings the lowest fares, and shoulder months such as October often price closer to low season than to peak. Sawa's prices do not change by season: Nile Majesty is from €610 and Nile Discovery from €500 in every month, as listed in November 2026.

faq.q: Is August too hot for a Nile cruise?
faq.a: It is the hottest month, with highs of about 41 to 42 °C in Luxor and Aswan, so August suits travellers who accept a dawn-to-noon sightseeing rhythm. Cruisers are generally air-conditioned and many have a pool for the afternoon. If sustained heat is not for you, choose March or November instead.

faq.q: What should I pack for a winter Nile cruise?
faq.a: Layers. December to February days reach 23 to 26 °C, which is t-shirt weather in the sun, but nights fall to 7 to 12 °C, and early-morning and evening deck time is genuinely cold. Bring a fleece for mornings and dinners, swimwear if your boat has a pool, and high-SPF sunscreen, because the winter sun is still strong.

faq.q: Can I pick my own Nile cruise date on Sawa?
faq.a: Yes. Pick the tour and the day and start your own date; Sawa reviews it before it opens for others to join. Reserving is free, and nothing is charged until four travellers have reserved the date (the GoAhead). The price is fixed per traveller; solo cabins are confirmed in the booking.

faq.q: What happens if my cruise departure doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A cruise date has until 30 days before departure to reach four travellers; if it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing and Sawa suggests other dates. Once confirmed, a date is not cancelled for low numbers and keeps running for the travellers who have paid.
